rv.q: He plays a cool hand in a sadly heavy-handed adaptation.
But it remains an oddly undramatic evening that, in strenuously seeking to mythologise Luke, undercuts his defiant humanity and simply makes him a rebel without a pause.
But such thematic blatancy is just one of this production’s many crimes.
The main problem with this brisk, trite reworking is that under Andrew Loudon's direction it lacks any sense of the menace and brutality that Pearce describes so vividly.

cn.t: Stage adaptation of the prison classic proves confusing and cliché-riddled, struggling to balance its hero as both rebel and saint. Marc Warren battles a weak script in this misguided return to the source novel.
